nodes.summary: For a finite abelian group $G$, a real number $\varepsilon$ and a natural number $k$, this is the number of $\varepsilon$-balanced $k$-element subsets of $G$ divided by the number of all $k$-element subsets of $G$, that is, the probability that a uniformly random $k$-element subset of $G$ is $\varepsilon$-balanced. When $k > |G|$ there are no $k$-element subsets and the value is $0$.

nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1179 (balanced subset sums of random subsets)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $N = |G|$ elements and let $\varepsilon$ be a real number. A subset $A \subseteq G$ is $\varepsilon$-balanced when, for every $g \in G$, the number $F_A(g)$ of subsets of $A$ whose elements sum to $g$ satisfies $\left| F_A(g) - 2^{|A|}/N \right| \le \varepsilon \cdot 2^{|A|}/N$.
nodes.title: $\varepsilon$-balanced subsets of a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: For a finite subset $A$ of an abelian group $G$ and an element $g \in G$, $F_A(g)$ is the number of subsets $S \subseteq A$, the empty set included, whose elements sum to $g$, that is, with $\sum_{x \in S} x = g$.
